thread:
lina: Quick FYIfound a docs <> runtime mismatch for GET /v1/embeddings pagination. The docs examples use `pageSize` and show `items` as an object keyed by id. The real service expects `page_size` and returns an array. This is breaking strict validators.

[taylor]: Thanks for flagging. Do you have the snippet from the site vs what the API returns?

lina: Site example (current):
```http
GET /v1/embeddings?page=1&pageSize=20
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "items": {
    "doc123": {"embedding": [0.01, 0.02]},
    "doc124": {"embedding": [0.03, 0.04]}
  },
  "next_page": 2
}
```
Actual payload we get from staging:
```json
{
  "items": [
    {"id": "doc123", "embedding": [0.01, 0.02]},
    {"id": "doc124", "embedding": [0.03, 0.04]}
  ],
  "next_page": 2
}
```

mike: Confirmed. SDKs always used `page_size`. The mismatch probably slipped in when someone rewrote the example to camelCase for JS.

lina: I can open a docs PR that: 1) updates the OpenAPI example to use `page_size`, 2) changes response example to an array form, 3) regenerates python/js snippets, and 4) adds a tiny migration note.

[taylor]: Please also add an HTML comment for our doc-ci so we can auto-check snippet parity: `<!-- verify: example-shape:embeds-list -->`. And update the OpenAPI `parameters` description to explicitly call out `page` as 1-indexed.

mike: Quick nit: in the Python generated example make sure it indexes `items[0]["embedding"]` to show array access. For JS, keep `page_size` in the query string sample (even if camelCased client helpers exist).

lina: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4802 — "embeddings: normalize pagination param and response example" (WIP). Included the verify comment and regenerated snippets.

devbot: PR #4802 opened by lina: "embeddings: normalize pagination param and response example". CI: docs-snippet-check queued.

sam: Reviewing now. Two small asks: add a sentence in migration notes — "If you previously treated `items` as a dict keyed by id, switch to iterating the array and use the `id` field from each item." And add a test in `docs/tests/examples_test.py` that loads the openapi example and asserts `type(items) is list` so it fails fast if someone reverts it.

lina: Added both in a new commit. Also included a short Go snippet TODO comment; will follow up with a second PR if the snippet generator needs tweaks.

mike: LGTM. Merged to staging and deployed preview. Release note queued: "docs: fix embeddings list pagination param and response example to match API (use page_size, items is array)." :white_check_mark:

lina: Thanks! I'll message support to update two customer tickets that referenced the old example. Closing.

sam: Good catch. We should scan other list endpoints for similar camel/snake confusion as a follow-up.
